literal: Even today, will it come? - that poverty which, even yesterday, killed me as it were.
translation: Will poverty, which felt as though it killed me even yesterday, come to torment me today as well?
modern: நேற்றும் என்னைக் கொன்றது போலத் துன்புறுத்திய வறுமை, இன்றும் என்னிடம் வருமோ?
explanation: This couplet vividly portrays the relentless, daily agony of extreme poverty. The speaker expresses dread, wondering if poverty—which inflicted such severe suffering yesterday that it felt like death—will return to torment them again today. By comparing the daily struggle of destitution to being killed repeatedly, the poet emphasizes that poverty is not a one-time hardship but a continuous, exhausting battle for survival.
